newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta minister says battles threaten gas price.
newsitem.headline: Alberta minister says battles threaten gas price.

text.p: Alberta Energy Minister Pat Black said on Monday that Canada's fractious natural gas producers and pipeline companies should quickly solve competition and tolling battles or face more depressed prices.

"We desparately need some takeaway capacity to meet market demands that are downstream, otherwise you're going to see depressed prices in Alberta for our gas," Black told reporters following a speech to an energy conference.
"I don't really care who builds the pipelines -- that's irrelevent to me."

Black's comments came after she served notice in December that the province would not jump in and force a government-mandated solution to battles over pipelines that would compete with NOVA Corp's system and how tolls are charged.

She said that with the current record level of drilling activity in Alberta, industry was taking the risk of vastly expanding production capacity while squabbling over pipeline space, which would leave gas trapped in the province.

NOVA, long the main mover of gas in Alberta, has said it was mulling several tolling options after it struck a deal with PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, which saw PanCanadian cancel a planned competing line but gain a cheaper "load-retention rate" toll."
Before the deal all Alberta producers paid the same to ship gas on the system, regardless of their location, with a "postage stamp" toll.

But other pipeline proposals are being considered, including the producer-backed Alliance Pipeline and Alberta Pipeline Project, sponsored by ATCO Ltd unit CU Gas, Shell Canada Ltd and Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd.

She said her Conservative government had not set any deadlines for industry to solve its problems and come forward with negotiated solutions. She also would not estimate when the squabbles would be over.

"There are proposals that are getting ready to go forward that makes it incumbent upon the industry to start focusing on the futre and doing it now," she said. "Why wait until your backs up against the wall?"
